entries.title: What BRC-20 is
entries.text: A fungible token protocol carried in Ordinals inscriptions. Bitcoin consensus validates none of it; the ledger is a replay of inscriptions by indexers.

entries.title: Account summary fact sheet
entries.text: Bitcoin mainnet, operations deploy mint transfer, 4-byte ticker, available and transferable balances, first is valid, originated by domo in March 2023.

entries.title: BRC-20 in Bitcoin Universe
entries.text: Inscribe supports deploy, mint and transfer. Wallet supports view, send and receive. Marketplace execution runs through the UniSat Marketplace Open API. Token explorer coverage is partial.

entries.title: Provenance and attribution
entries.text: BRC-20 was created by domo on 8 March 2023 and released as a public experiment. Layer1 Foundation maintains the indexing rules; OPI is the reference implementation.

entries.title: Carrier and encoding
entries.text: One UTF-8 JSON object inscribed as text/plain or application/json in an ord envelope. Every protocol value is a JSON string.

entries.title: Identifiers: ticker, inscription ID, address
entries.text: Ticker is exactly 4 UTF-8 bytes, compared case-insensitively. Balance identity is the output script holding the inscribed satoshi.

entries.title: deploy fields
entries.text: p, op, tick and max are required; lim, dec and self_mint are optional. max is the immutable maximum supply, lim the per-mint limit, dec the divisibility from 0 to 18.

entries.title: mint fields
entries.text: p, op, tick and amt are required. amt must be positive, at most lim, with decimals fitting dec.

entries.title: transfer fields
entries.text: p, op, tick and amt are required. amt must not exceed the available balance at confirmation.

entries.title: R3: every value must be a JSON string
entries.text: A JSON number, boolean or null in any protocol field makes the operation invalid. Unquoted max is the classic mistake.

entries.title: R7: ticker byte length
entries.text: tick must be exactly 4 UTF-8 bytes, or 5 bytes for a self-mint deploy. The limit counts bytes, not characters.

entries.title: R10: first is valid
entries.text: The first valid confirmed deploy of a ticker owns it. Later deploys of the same ticker are ignored and deploy economics are immutable.

entries.title: R11: amount grammar and decimals
entries.text: Base-10 only, no sign, no exponent, no leading zeros, no separators. Fractional digits after trimming trailing zeros must not exceed dec.

entries.title: R14: the mint remainder rule
entries.text: A mint that crosses the maximum supply is credited only the remaining amount. Once supply is exhausted every later mint is invalid.

entries.title: R16 to R21: two-phase transfer rules
entries.text: Inscribing reserves the amount from available to transferable. The inscription is one-use: its first spend settles it to a recipient, back to self, or as fee.

entries.title: R24: cursed inscriptions
entries.text: Inscriptions assigned negative numbers under the Ordinals rules are not valid BRC-20 operations.

entries.title: State transitions
entries.text: Overall balance equals available plus transferable. Mint credits available; inscribing a transfer reclassifies available as transferable; the first spend settles it.

entries.title: Invalid conditions
entries.text: Content that is not JSON or lacks the brc-20 protocol tag is not a BRC-20 inscription. Everything else that breaks a rule is a recognized but ineffective operation.

entries.title: Extensions: self-mint and programmable
entries.text: Deploys with self_mint true may claim 5-byte tickers and only the deployer may mint them. Programmable extensions are out of scope.

entries.title: Universe indexing decisions
entries.text: Atomic integer arithmetic, transactional invariant enforcement, lowercased ticker identity with preserved display casing, partial coverage, classic operations only.

entries.title: The mental model
entries.text: Nothing validates at signing time, order decides ownership, and moving a satoshi can move a balance.

entries.title: Deploying a ticker
entries.text: Worked deploy example for ordi with max 21000000 and lim 1000. Deployers get no premine and economics can never be changed.

entries.title: Minting
entries.text: Worked mint example and the four checks an indexer applies, including the remainder rule on the last mint.

entries.title: The two-phase transfer
entries.text: Sending BRC-20 takes two transactions. Phase one reserves the amount; phase two spends the inscription and settles it. Worked example sending 100 ordi from Alice to Bob.

entries.title: How balances get lost
entries.text: A wallet unaware of inscriptions can spend a transfer inscription as change or fee, settling it against whoever receives it.

entries.title: Bitcoin Universe support matrix
entries.text: Inscribe deploy, mint and transfer; wallet view, send and receive; marketplace listing and buying through UniSat; offers not supported; token explorer coverage partial.

entries.title: Terminology
entries.text: Definitions of inscription, reveal transaction, ticker, available, transferable and overall balance, transfer inscription, atomic amount, checkpoint, cursed inscription.

entries.title: Confirmation semantics
entries.text: Validity is decided at confirmation against the confirmed ledger. Same-block operations apply in transaction order. A void transfer inscription never revives.

entries.title: Mempool semantics
entries.text: Unconfirmed operations are not protocol state and must never satisfy a precondition. Universe publishes partial coverage because there is no exhaustive BRC-20 mempool feed.

entries.title: Reorg semantics
entries.text: State after a reorg must equal a clean replay of the new chain. Reversal must be complete, dependencies must unwind together, and reorgs crossing the finalized height are refused.

entries.title: The cursed inscriptions caveat
entries.text: Which inscriptions are cursed depends on the ord version, so an Ordinals upgrade can change historical BRC-20 answers. Pin the version and reindex.

entries.title: Amounts and arithmetic
entries.text: Scale to integers at dec and never leave integer arithmetic. Reject values above uint64 maximum 18446744073709551615 and use wider types for aggregates.

entries.title: Fee and size considerations
entries.text: A payload is 60 to 80 witness bytes. Every operation costs a commit and reveal; a transfer takes three transactions end to end. Invalid operations cost the same as valid ones.

entries.title: Limitations
entries.text: No consensus enforcement, possible indexer divergence, no atomic swaps, no protocol-level offers, ticker squatting, irreversible economics.

entries.title: Security considerations
entries.text: Accidental spends of transfer inscriptions, ticker impersonation, indexer trust, marketplace listing evidence, reorg exposure, defensive parsing.

entries.title: Implementation checklist
entries.text: Sixteen steps from pinning the Ordinals version through strict parsing, integer arithmetic, two transfer events, reorg reversal, and verification against test vectors.

entries.title: Valid payload vectors
entries.text: Six valid payloads: classic deploy, deploy with decimals, mint, transfer, self-mint 5-byte deploy, and a formatted payload with unknown keys.

entries.title: Invalid payload vectors
entries.text: Fourteen invalid payloads: numeric fields, wrong protocol tag, uppercase op, wrong ticker length, dec above 18, lim above max, zero amount, excess decimals, uint64 overflow, leading zeros, missing amt, malformed JSON, array payload.

entries.title: Ledger vector: first is valid
entries.text: A duplicate deploy of the same ticker in a later block is ignored and mints apply against the first deploy's limits.

entries.title: Ledger vector: the mint remainder rule
entries.text: The mint that crosses maximum supply is credited only the remainder, not rejected and not credited in full.

entries.title: Ledger vector: two-phase transfer outcomes
entries.text: Postings for recipient, self and fee spends from the same starting balance, and the inert second spend.

entries.title: Ledger vector: reorg reversal
entries.text: Orphaned blocks are reversed completely and the replacement chain is replayed, producing state identical to a clean replay.

entries.title: Inscription payload validator
entries.text: Paste a BRC-20 inscription JSON payload and see every check explained with its rule. Runs entirely in your browser; nothing is transmitted or stored.

entries.title: What the validator cannot check
entries.text: Chain-dependent conditions: whether the ticker is deployed, the deployed limit and decimals, remaining supply, available balance, and the inscription envelope.

entries.title: Documentation versions
entries.text: Version 1.0.0 rebuilt the site as a full protocol dossier on 2026-09-01, replacing the 0.1.0 single-page introduction.

entries.title: Protocol milestones
entries.text: domo publishes BRC-20 and the ordi deploy on 8 March 2023; the Layer1 Foundation maintains the indexing rules; the self-issuance extension admits 5-byte tickers.
